function.mechanism: Imparts yellow-orange color via azo chromophore absorbance in the visible spectrum (inference from azo structure and regulatory color-additive classification).

adi.basis: EFSA 2014 reconsideration concluded refined exposure was of no concern and that the temporary ADI of 1 mg/kg bw/day should be considered final.

efsa.key_finding: No concern at refined exposure estimates versus ADI; 2009 EFSA had identified potential concern for children under conservative MPL exposure assumptions.

fda.notes: Listed as FD&C Yellow No. 6, subject to batch certification (part 80), permitted for foods including dietary supplements under GMP, with standard-of-identity limitations; no separate GRAS listing identified for this color additive in Title 21.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database entry (2011) states ADI 0-4 mg/kg bw and withdrawal of prior 0-2.5 mg/kg bw ADI.

concerns.summary: In vitro human lymphocyte studies and some in vivo rodent studies report chromosomal damage/comet-assay signals, especially at higher concentrations or in combination exposures.
A rat study reported oxidative-stress linked hepatic/renal toxicity markers and histopathological changes after oral exposure.
Human RCT evidence shows hyperactivity effects from mixtures of artificial colors/preservative; attribution to E110 alone is uncertain.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2014 refined exposure assessment found no concern compared with ADI 1 mg/kg bw/day.
JECFA 2011 concluded dietary exposure to Sunset Yellow FCF does not present a health concern.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2009 reported concern under MPL-based scenarios in children; EFSA 2014 refined exposure assessment reduced concern.

risk_assessment.rationale: E110 remains approved by EFSA/FDA/JECFA with explicit ADIs and no IARC listing, but the evidence base includes credible experimental genotoxic/organ-toxicity signals and child-focused behavioral concern in color-additive mixtures; exposure-risk conclusions differ between conservative and refined assessments.
key_factors: EFSA final ADI 1 mg/kg bw/day with refined exposure no-concern outcome
JECFA ADI 0-4 mg/kg bw and no-health-concern conclusion
US approval as certified color additive under 21 CFR 74.706
Pediatric behavioral signal from mixed-additive trial
